text:
alex: quick idea — instead of a big global cutover for v2 -> v3, what if we do tiny staggered cohorts by customer size + traffic profile?

maria: can you sketch what a "cohort" looks like operationally? small weekly windows? opt-in?

alex: yep. tentative plan: 1) auto-detect low-risk tenants (low qps, simple routes) -> migrate first 2) invite mid-tier by opt-in with throttled traffic mirror 3) then forced cutover windows for high-volume accounts with SRE support.

sam: sounds reasonable. metrics we need: error delta, latency p50/p95, token cost delta, and customer-facing regression rate.

jordan: how long per cohort? we should avoid long tails — maybe 7 days monitoring + rollback window, but faster for super-low-risk.

alex: agreed. propose schedule prototype in a table:
```
cohort A: 100 tenants (tails < 10qps)  -> 48h canary + 6d monitor
cohort B: 50 tenants (100-500qps) -> 72h canary + 7d monitor + scaled rollback runbook
cohort C: 10 tenants (>500qps) -> scheduled maintenance window + 14d monitor + on-call squeeze
```

pat: two operational questions: 1) who flips the cohort flag? 2) what telemetry gate triggers rollback?

alex: (1) flips via console or infra runbook (needs two approvals for cohort C). (2) rollback triggers: +5% error rate or +50ms p95 sustained for >10m, or model-quality alerts tied to prompt harness.

maria: do we want a lightweight compatibility middleware for the first two cohorts to rewrite a couple of deprecated fields server-side? avoids client churn.

sam: that middleware is fine but make it short-lived. add telemetry tag so we can remove and measure how many clients relied on it.

jordan: coverage note — we must run the regression eval suite on representative tenant prompts before cohort join. otherwise we'll be blind.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled: canary job queued for cohort A at 2026-04-05T02:00Z — notify #eng-runtime when job starts. :robot_face:

pat: also need a migration CLI for customers who want to opt-in early and a guest-token flow for testing. docs + SDK snippet required.

alex: +1 on CLI. I'll draft a short CLI UX and a telemetry table for the rollback gates. keeping it minimal so we don't create more long-lived shims.

maria: one more thing — budget impact. we need an estimate of token-cost delta for v3 (quantized vs full) per cohort so billing can sync.

sam: I'll run traffic-sim on staging to estimate cost change and push numbers by EOD tomorrow.

jordan: thanks — if we can get staging sims + evals done this week we can lock cohort A for next week.

alex: cool. action items: alex -> CLI + runbook draft, sam -> traffic sims + cost numbers, maria -> telemetry gating matrix, jordan -> eval harness runs, pat -> docs & opt-in flow. I'll create a short RFC follow-up doc after sims land. :thumbsup:
